measures_taken: Bangladesh authorities and local communities responded; a joint UN/Government assessment mission supported response planning and environmental assessment.
preventive_measures: Suggested lesson: review vessel-collision risks and strengthen spill preparedness. This is a general recommendation, not a claim that the source prescribed this exact measure.

cause_category: Bunkering / valve opened before hose connection
oil_type: RMG 380 / No. 6 fuel oil (heavy fuel oil)
spill_quantity_unit: barrel into water (NOAA report; about 3 barrels spilled onto barge deck)
measures_taken: U.S. Coast Guard Federal On-Scene Coordinator authorized a surface-washing agent; responders were to monitor and collect data. NOAA and the Regional Response Team were notified and supported as needed.
preventive_measures: The report says a valve was accidentally opened before the transfer hose was connected. Practical lesson: verify valve position and hose connection before opening transfer valves. This lesson is inferred from the documented cause.

incident_name: LPG carrier HSFO overflow during bunkering (MAIB Safety Digest)
cause_category: Bunkering / tank overfill / valve alignment failure
spill_quantity_unit: litres (estimated; source says up to 2,000 litres)
measures_taken: Crew ordered bunkering stopped and activated the emergency response team; about 1 tonne was recovered from the deck; contaminated absorbent material was removed by garbage boat.
preventive_measures: The report found a valve jammed by debris and another not fully tightened, allowing oil into a tank already about 80% full. Lesson: verify valve alignment and closure, tank capacity and level monitoring before and during transfer; check valves for obstruction.

measures_taken: Emergency response and cleanup operations were conducted in wetlands, Talmadge Creek and the Kalamazoo River; local residents self-evacuated. Cleanup continued for an extended period.
preventive_measures: NTSB identified corrosion-fatigue cracks, deficient integrity-management procedures and delayed detection. Explicit lesson: improve pipeline integrity management, defect assessment, leak detection and operator response to abnormal conditions.

measures_taken: The leak was responded to and environmental remediation was undertaken; the NTSB investigated the release and its cause.
preventive_measures: NTSB found erosion caused by water jet impingement from a nearby leaking water pipe, with cathodic-protection interference contributing. Lesson: control third-party utility installation near pipelines and assess corrosion protection and external interference risks.

incident_name: T/V Krymsk bunker-fuel leak, Gulf of Mexico
spill_quantity_unit: gallons at risk (NOAA record; actual released amount not confirmed in this initial report)
measures_taken: U.S. Coast Guard responded; vessel crew were transferring fuel from the leaking tank to another tank to secure the source. NOAA supported the federal on-scene coordinator; dispersants were reported as applied.
preventive_measures: The initial record attributes the leak to collision damage to a fuel tank. Lesson inferred: assess tank integrity after contact and promptly isolate/transfer fuel from damaged tanks. Actual quantity spilled is not established by this source.

incident_name: Cosco Busan fuel-oil spill, San Francisco Bay
spill_quantity_unit: gallons (NTSB report describes approximately 53,500 gallons; estimates differed during response)
measures_taken: U.S. Coast Guard and California spill investigators boarded the vessel and assessed fuel loss; unified response organizations mobilized recovery resources and environmental response operations.
preventive_measures: The NTSB investigation identified navigation, bridge-resource management and safety-management issues. For spill prevention, maintain effective navigation procedures and promptly communicate verified spill estimates to the unified response command.

incident_name: Piney Point oil pipeline rupture, Maryland
cause_category: Pipeline rupture / missed defect in inspection data
measures_taken: Environmental response and cleanup operations were carried out in surrounding wetlands, Swanson Creek and the Patuxent River.
preventive_measures: NTSB found a pipe fracture that was missed because in-line inspection data were interpreted inaccurately. Lesson: validate inspection-tool interpretations and investigate anomalies rather than dismissing uncertain indications.

incident_name: Lakehead Pipeline rupture, Grand Rapids, Minnesota
spill_quantity_unit: barrels (revised company estimate reported by NOAA)
measures_taken: The company shut the pipeline valve; about 300 nearby residents were evacuated. U.S. Coast Guard, EPA, state pollution-control and emergency agencies responded; booms, skimmers and vacuum trucks were among response resources noted by NOAA.
preventive_measures: NOAA notes that shutdown took almost an hour after notification and that the delay likely increased the spill. Lesson: make leak detection, escalation and pipeline isolation fast and reliable.

incident_name: M/V Lavaux bunkering spill, Long Beach Harbor
spill_quantity_unit: gallons (NOAA record also describes approximately 30 barrels)
measures_taken: The vessel master contacted the U.S. Coast Guard; a contractor installed containment boom around the vessel, barge and nearby breakwater. Cleanup continued, a boom watch was deployed, and later surveys checked for remaining oil.
preventive_measures: The NOAA record does not specify a confirmed technical root cause or formal recommendations. General lesson, not attributed as a source finding: use transfer checklists, active watchkeeping and immediately available containment equipment.

cause_category: Pipeline leak / weld fracture near flange
oil_type: Monterey crude mixed with drilling and pumping water
spill_quantity_unit: barrels (revised estimate; initial 2,900 barrels was potential pipeline volume, not final spill estimate)
measures_taken: Skimming vessels were contracted for on-water recovery; dispersant aircraft were alerted but not used. Federal agencies supported and oversaw the operator-led response, including wildlife and shoreline observation.
preventive_measures: The documented cause was a fracture in a weld near a flange. Lesson inferred: inspect and maintain pipeline welds and flange-adjacent sections; distinguish potential pipeline inventory from confirmed released volume.

oil_type: Crude oil (reported as South Louisiana crude)
spill_quantity_unit: barrels (NOAA's detailed report; initial notification mentioned 10 barrels)
measures_taken: The pipeline was shut in, oil-spill response organizations were dispatched, and Coast Guard pollution responders were sent. On-water recovery and shoreline cleanup were recorded as applied.
preventive_measures: The source attributes the release to a dredge striking an underwater pipeline. Lesson inferred: map and mark underwater pipelines, communicate their locations to marine works, and verify clearance before dredging.

incident_name: La Pampilla refinery / Mare Doricum spill, Peru
cause_category: Oil transfer / broken underwater pipeline manifold
measures_taken: Peruvian response authorities received support from a U.S. National Response Team delegation. NOAA specialists supported satellite analysis, oil trajectory prediction, remediation planning, oiled-wildlife response and emergency management. On-water recovery and shoreline cleanup were recorded as applied.
preventive_measures: The cause of the broken manifold was listed as under investigation in the NOAA record. No specific preventive finding is asserted here; use this case as an example where root-cause information was not yet confirmed in the cited source.

incident_name: Eagle Otome collision, Port Arthur, Texas
spill_quantity_unit: gallons spilled into water (NTSB states 862,344 gallons released from tank, with an estimated 462,000 gallons entering water)
measures_taken: Pollution response procedures were initiated while the three vessels remained together in the canal; response agencies worked on containment and recovery.
preventive_measures: NTSB identified failure to correct the tanker’s sheering motion and a late turn as the probable cause of the collision. Lessons include safer navigation decisions and procedures that reduce collision risk around loaded tankers.
